Direction is named in advance: it inflates momentum more than buy-and-hold, so a PASS here would be suspect while a FAIL is if anything understated.
Benign period. 2014-2019 contains no COVID crash and no 2022 bear market, which flatters any long-only trend rule.

A PASS would still not be permission to enable anything. It would be one period, one parameterisation, and would need the full walk-forward and the live gate before it meant anything.
spec.prior: EDGE claims stand at 0 for 7 entering this test. spec.title: Pre-specified cross-sectional momentum (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993), no selection

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP, and it is severe here — worse than in any previous section. The universe is screened from TODAY'S S&P 1500 membership, so every company that went bankrupt or was delisted in the 2008 crisis is absent by construction. The crash is therefore systematically softened, and long-only momentum benefits most from that. Direction named in advance: this inflates every arm, so a PASS here would be weak evidence while a FAIL is strong.

The screen measures liquidity on the FIRST calendar year only (2007), so universe selection cannot peek at the test window. That is a guard, not a guarantee: 2007 liquidity itself reflects pre-crisis conditions.

Three arms share a snapshot and a universe, so their results are strongly correlated. "All three moved" is therefore much weaker evidence than three independent confirmations, and must not be read as such.
Low trade count. A top-decile rule places few trades, so per-arm confidence intervals will be wide and an INCONCLUSIVE significance result is not support.

A PASS is not permission to enable anything. It would be one family, one period, one universe construction — and it would still owe a walk-forward on a period with no survivorship advantage before it meant anything.
spec.prior: This fails. EDGE claims stand at 0 for 8, and §35 already ran xsmom-12-1 on 2014-2019 where it lost 4.04% while the market gained 90.41%. The reason to run it anyway is that 2007-2013 is the first period this repository has ever scored that contains a real bear market, and §35's registration named "benign period" as a failure mode that has stood unanswered since. A three-arm family requirement also makes a lucky single-arm result impossible to mistake for an effect. If momentum has any regime in which it earns its keep, a crisis is the most-claimed one; if it fails here too, that claim is answered on this repository's own data rather than by assertion.
spec.title: Cross-sectional momentum family coherence, 2007-2013 (incl. the GFC)

failure_modes: PERIOD ALREADY MINED. §32 scored 2020-2026 with these families. This is a subset. Any result is a re-description of spent evidence and must never be cited as confirmation of §37 — two readings of overlapping data are not two independent results.

Survivorship again, though far milder than §37's: the universe is today's index membership screened on 2022 liquidity, so recent delistings are absent. Over four years that matters much less than over the 2008 crisis.
A short window. 2022-2026 is ~4.5 years and contains one bear market (2022) followed by a long recovery, so it is close to a single regime.

The strongest temptation this file must resist: if these arms happen to look good here while failing in §37, that is the textbook shape of a period-specific fluke, and §34 already established this repository cannot tell such a fluke from an effect. It would be a reason to distrust the number, not to enable anything.
spec.prior: No expectation is recorded, because a prior is what makes a test falsifiable and this is not a test. §32 already rejected these families on a period that contains this one, so the answer is substantially known and stating a confident prior would be dressing foreknowledge as prediction. What this actually buys is comparability: identical arms and pass mark against §37, so the difference between a crisis period and a recent one can be read directly. If §37's monotone damage by lookback also appears here, that consistency is worth knowing; if it does not, the instability across regimes is itself the observation, and it is the same instability §34 found when no selector could beat a coin.
spec.title: Momentum family on 2022-2026 — DIAGNOSTIC, decides nothing (§32 already mined this period)

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP, severe. The universe is today's S&P 1500 membership screened on 2000 liquidity, so the dot-com casualties are absent by construction — the companies that went to zero between 2000 and 2002 were never fetched. This flatters ANY long strategy including the incumbent, so a FAIL here is strong evidence and a PASS is weak. Same direction as §37, same asymmetry.

The strategies were tuned on 2020-2026 38-symbol data (§14-§29). Running them on a 500-symbol universe from a different era changes two things at once, so a poor result cannot be attributed to the period alone — the breadth of the universe is a confound and is not being controlled here.

Low deployment makes `beats_exposure_matched` easy in a way that is arithmetically correct and substantively hollow: a bot 92% in cash faces a bar of 8% of the market's return. Clause (d) stops the degenerate case, but a marginal PASS at very low deployment should be read as "it barely invested", not as "it has edge".

2000-2006 contains a crash and a full recovery, which is a favourable shape for a long-only rules engine measured on total return. A single period cannot separate skill from having been pointed at a rising 2003-2006.
A PASS would NOT mean the live bot is working. It would mean one configuration cleared one gate on one unseen period, and it would still owe the live 30-trade evidence gate before anything changed.
spec.prior: The incumbent probably fails, and the reason is already written into this file rather than being a hunch. The ALREADY-SEEN OBSERVATION recorded before this registration shows the same test applied to three periods whose numbers were produced as baselines for other claims: 2007-2013 fails (+0.78% against a +9.65% bar), 2022-2026 fails (-11.62% against +3.75%), and 2014-2019 passes by 1.44pp at 70% deployment. spec.title: Does the live ensemble clear its own enablement gate on 2000-2006?

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP. The universe is today's index membership screened on early liquidity, so companies that failed during the dot-com crash and recovery are absent by construction. This flatters any long strategy, and it flatters the DECAY arm more than the baseline, because the decay arm holds more and for longer. A PASS is therefore weaker evidence here than a FAIL is.

The decay parameters were chosen for roundness, not fitted — but they were chosen by someone who had already read §40's census. Grace 10 and half-life 20 are not innocent of that knowledge, only of any candidate run. A PASS should not be read as "these are the right numbers", only as "these numbers did not make risk worse".

Clause (d) is non-binding on s41c and near-certain on the other three. It proves the latch lifted; it proves nothing about whether lifting it helped. Reading a PASS on (d) as a result would be reading the thermometer as the weather.

More deployment means more exposure to the market's own direction. On a period whose market rose, the decay arm will look better for reasons that have nothing to do with the rail. Return is deliberately not a clause for exactly this reason, and any write-up that quotes the return difference as evidence is misreading this spec.

A PASS on all four does NOT mean the bot should trade live at these settings. It means one mechanical defect has been repaired without making measured risk worse. The 30-closed-trade live evidence gate is untouched and the live record is still two closed trades.
spec.prior: The deployment clause should pass on 2000-2006 and the risk clauses are the real question. §40 measured the mechanism directly rather than inferring it, so there is little doubt the latch is what holds deployment at 8.07%; the open question is what the bot does with capital once it can use it. The honest expectation is that maxdd_within is the clause most likely to fail: a bot that re-enters after a drawdown is a bot that can take a second drawdown, and 3.0pp is not a generous allowance. Clause (b) is the one I would least like to see fail, because a significantly worse per-trade P&L at higher deployment would say the rail had been carrying the strategy rather than strangling it — that the bot was only profitable when it was barely trading, which is not a strategy. This is a CAPACITY claim and cannot show edge; ten EDGE claims have been rejected and this one does not touch that record.

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP, severe, and it flatters the incumbent here exactly as it did in §37 and §39. The universe is today's S&P 1500 screened on then-current liquidity, so companies that went to zero were never fetched. A FAIL is therefore strong evidence and a PASS is weak — the asymmetry runs the same way in all four periods.

The judge model reproduces a DISTRIBUTION, not decisions. It cannot recover which trades the real judge would have cut, and its calibration rests on 164 decisions over 12 live days in one regime, heavily serially correlated, so the effective sample is far below 164 and the tails are unmeasured. This simulator is closer to live than a judge-less one — that is the bar it has to clear — not accurate in a way it has not earned.

The strategies were tuned on 38 symbols of 2020-2026 data. Running them on a 500-symbol universe across 26 years changes period AND breadth at once, so a failure cannot be attributed to the period alone. Breadth is an uncontrolled confound and is not being controlled here either.

Low deployment makes beats_exposure_matched arithmetically easy and substantively hollow — a bot 90% in cash faces a bar of 10% of the market's return. Clause (d) blocks the degenerate case, but a marginal PASS at low deployment must be read as "it barely invested", never as "it has edge".

I computed the expected clause outcomes from §42's census BEFORE registering this. That makes the prior sharp, and it also means a result matching the prediction is weaker evidence than it looks: I already knew the inputs. The genuinely new information in this run is the enablement_gate clause, which is not computable from the census, and any cell that DISAGREES with the prediction.

A PASS anywhere would NOT mean the live bot works. It would mean one configuration cleared one gate on one period, and it would still owe the live evidence gate — 30 closed trades and 3 months — of which the paper ledger currently holds TWO closed trades.
spec.prior: This is predicted to FAIL, and the prediction is arithmetic rather than a hunch. §42's census — already published, judge on, same shipped config — gives return, buy-and-hold and average deployment for every period, and clause (b)'s bar is computable from them before this runs. Those computed bars are: 2000-2006 +9.45% against +29.02%; 2007-2013 +2.42% against +10.10%; 2014-2019 +56.71% against +62.61%; 2022-2026 -7.71% against +2.13%. So (b) is expected to fail in ALL FOUR, and (a) additionally on the profit-factor floor in three (1.122, 1.082, 0.367 against the 1.3 minimum; only 2014-2019's 1.396 clears it). (c) beats_buy_hold is expected to fail everywhere and is the least interesting of the four. (d) min_trades should pass everywhere. THE CELL THAT MATTERS IS 2014-2019. It is the ONLY period in which this bot has ever cleared its own gate — §35 recorded it passing the exposure-matched bar, and on the judge-off census it clears by +6.66pp. With the judge modelled it is predicted to FAIL by -5.90pp: return drops 69.02% -> 56.71% while deployment barely moves, so the bar stays put and the bot falls under it. If that flip reproduces, the single pass in this project's history was an artifact of a simulator that did not model a component the live bot has been running for weeks, and the honest count becomes ZERO periods in four. Stating it this precisely is the point: this prior is falsifiable to within a fraction of a percentage point, and if the run disagrees with these numbers then something in my understanding of the machine is wrong and THAT is the finding. A PASS anywhere would be genuinely surprising and would need explaining before it was believed.
